To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the M74 mortality syndrome in Baltic salmon fry is associated with thiamine deficiency in the developing yolk-sac embryo, and that the syndrome can be prevented by treating the female broodstock in the rivers with thiamine or by treating the fry with thiamine.

(i) bathing of yolk-sacs in thiamine HCL solution is an effective treatment against M74 syndrome, (ii) a single intraperitonial injection of thiamin to female salmon in the summer before the next spawning season is also effective against M74 syndrome and (iii) astaxanthin injections to female salmon in summer do not prevent yolk-sac mortalities.
Thiamine hydrochlorid (vitamin B1) treatment of wild female Baltic salmon before spawning is an effective way to prevent yolk-sac mortalities (M74 syndrome) of their progeny in the rivers.
